newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FCC okays plans to wire schools to Internet.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FCC okays plans to wire schools to Internet.

text.p: The Federal Communications Commission Wednesday voted to spend $2.3 billion a year to wire schools and libraries to the Internet.
The agency also voted to spend about $400 million to link rural health care providers to the global computer network.
The FCC rules also are designed to ensure affordable phone service for Americans in high-cost rural areas and those in low-income communities.
Eligible schools and libraries could buy access to the Internet at discounts of 20 percent to 90 percent under the rules, which stem from last year's communcations laws.
Funds to support the plan will be collected from telecommunications companies.
Internet service providers will not be required to contribute to the funding.
Funding for schools and libraries will begin in January of 1998.
